title: Type errors caused by circular references to autoloaded scene
body:
### Tested versions

- Discovered in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sonoma (14.6.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 Max (Apple8) - Apple M2 Max (12 threads)

### Issue description

When there are two globals that reference each other with one of them being an autoloaded scene, references to the scene are treated as the "Node" type rather than as the type of script attached to the root node.

When running `empty_scene.tscn` from the example project, the following warning should appear:

```
W 0:00:00:286   The property "test_value" is not present on the inferred type "Node" (but may be present on a subtype).
  <GDScript Error>UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS
  <GDScript Source>test_global2.gd:6
```

### Steps to reproduce

The provided project consists of the following two scripts. `test_global.gd` is attached to the root node of a scene, `TestGlobal.tscn`, which is autoloaded. `test_global2.gd` is autoloaded without being attached to a scene. The type error will appear when any scene is run regardless of if it contains scripts that reference either of the globals.

```
# test_global.gd
extends Node2D

@export var test_value: String

func _ready() -> void:
	print(TestGlobal2.test_value)
```

```
# test_global2.gd
extends Node2D

@export var test_value: String

func _ready() -> void:
	print(TestGlobal.test_value)
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[globalsdebug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19827123/globalsdebug.zip)
